newsitem.title: USA: McDermott comfortable with '98 EPS consensus.
newsitem.headline: McDermott comfortable with '98 EPS consensus.

text.p: NEW ORLEANS, June 11 Reuter) - McDermott International Inc said on Wednesday that it was comfortable with analyst forecasts of 1998 earnings per share of $0.90 before any extraordinary items and with forecasts of $1.47 per share for its J. Ray McDermott subsidiary.

The company said in a statement after meeting analysts and shareholders about the alleged wrongdoings at the company by employees of J. Ray McDermott that the subsidiary had a work backlog worth $1.8 billion, including about 75 percent of the subsidiary's anticipated fiscal 1998 work.
The parent company backlog of orders is $4.2 billion at end-March 1997 and this figure includes 70 percent of the anticipated 1998 orders, the company said.
McDermott shares were off 3/8 at 27-3/4 after the news.

"These bookings put a substantial amount of our volume for fiscal 1998 in our backlog and give us confidence that we can achieve our financial goals for the year," said Roger Tetrault, McDermott International's chief executive officer.
Both companies have passed resolutions demanding officers own stock valued at a multiple of their annual salaries.

Details of irregularities concerning employees at the overseas operations of both McDermott companies surfaced in April and the company said then that J. Ray expected to report a net loss of $60-$70 million for the fourth quarter of this year.
In order to drag J. Ray McDermott back to profit it will sell operations outside its core marine and power business.
No details on proposed sales were immediately available.
Tetrault said the principal focus of the allegations remains on a portion of J. Ray McDermott's business and the allegations could result in criminal or civil liabilities.

As part of its restructuring, McDermott International plans to cut general and administrative expenses to $53 million in 1998 from $67 million this year and it said the parent would report a loss of $180-$200 million in the fourth quarter.

But McDermott said that a company hotline set up to get details of any wrongdoing had "received no substantial information". Tetrault said the company has notified the appropriate authorities concerning the investigation, but added, "the company is not currently at liberty to identify those authorities".
